description: The Settings dialog's Access page (Baude's, Record's and the phone's; on the phone the fifth page of Settings, switched to by the bar at its foot): for the host picked beside New session, who in the mesh may use each of its capabilities, read and write apart where a capability has both, as it answers access. The host enforces each rule on the wire ops the capability uses (baudelib/access.py, PhoneAccess.kt): a member it refuses is answered access_denied, and a head on the host's own machine, or over ssh, is never refused. Who's asking comes from the signed open of the member's tunnel (mesh.py), or, for a chat's own tools, the member that started the chat.
opens: Settings… → Access (the dialog's page switcher; the phone's: the bar at Settings' foot)

parts.name: Host
parts.shows: Row "Host" with the picked host's name after it (dim), as Telemetry's.

parts.name: Capability rows
parts.shows: One boxed list, a row for each capability in this order: Shell, Emission Browser, Providers, Model Files, Agent Spawn, Agent Management, Kubernetes, Databases, Subscriptions, Access Rules. A capability with one rule (Shell, Providers, Model Files, Agent Spawn, Databases) is its name and one button after it naming who may. A capability split into read and write (Emission Browser, Agent Management, Kubernetes, Subscriptions, Access Rules) is its name over two compact lines in the same row, "Read" and "Write" (dim, a little in from the name), each with its rule's button at the row's end, so every button sits in one column at any width. A button names who may: Everybody, Nobody, the members' names (one or two), or "<n> members". It opens the checklist the sessions' Groups and Kubernetes' Namespaces have: a check "Everybody" over a check for each member the host can name (those it reaches, has lately, or a rule names). Every member checked is Everybody, none is Nobody, some is those members. With no other member, "No other members" dim under Everybody. A host without all of a capability's rules (older code) has that row hidden. A row the asking app may not change (editable false: a member Access Rules' Write refuses) has its buttons greyed.

actions.by: check or uncheck in the button's list
actions.does: Sends access_set at once (capability: the rule's name, e.g. kube_write; rule: everybody, nobody, or chosen with the members checked) and shows the capability's rules as the host answers; checking Everybody checks every member, unchecking it unchecks every one. Write lets a member read too, and the host keeps the two together: whoever Write is given to is added to Read, and whoever Read loses is taken out of Write, so both buttons always say who may. A refusal says "Couldn't change access: <why>" in a toast and the row goes back to what the host has.

decisions.said: The owner wants to configure who may use each of a host's capabilities from the mesh: everybody, nobody, or chosen principals; shell through Multiplex, the Emission browser, providers, model files, agent spawn, managing existing agents, Kubernetes and databases (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has an Access page after Telemetry: a row for each capability with Everybody / Nobody / Chosen Members, the members chosen by switches; the host keeps the rules and enforces them on the wire, never only in the UI

decisions.said: The UI for this should be in Settings (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Access rules are set in Settings → Access on every app, for the host picked beside New session

decisions.said: The Access Rules capability defaults to Nobody: only local and ssh heads change rules until members are listed (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Access Rules starts at Nobody; every other capability at Everybody

decisions.said: A rule is only as good as its weakest path; who is asking must come from the authenticated link, not a claim a member can forge (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every op reaching a capability's effect is guarded by it (reading a chat's folder, git and @ names by Agent Management, Kubernetes and databases parts of @ by theirs, host-admin ops by Access Rules, subscription accounts and sign-in by Subscriptions, approving commands by Shell, Bots by Shell and Emission Browser), and members are told by their signed keys

decisions.said: Each capability showing two dropdowns (a mode dropdown and the expander's) is odd; Everybody / Nobody / chosen members should be read off a group-like list (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app gives an access rule one control: a button naming who may, opening a checklist with Everybody over a check per member (the Groups and Namespaces checklist); all checked is Everybody, none Nobody, some those members. No separate mode dropdown, no expander

decisions.said: Signing in to a subscription from another host was refused as Access Rules; access policy isn't subscription management, and the owner wants to allow managing subscriptions while still stopping another host from changing the other policies (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every host has a Subscriptions capability of its own, its row before Access Rules: listing, adding, renaming, removing (signing out of) and picking subscription accounts, reading their usage, signing in and passing sign-in codes (accounts, login, login_code), and moving a chat to another subscription (with the chat's Agent Management too). Access Rules covers changing rules and the host's own admin only, never subscriptions. Subscriptions starts at Everybody, as every capability but Access Rules does, since mesh membership is trust and a member that may start chats already spends the host's subscriptions

decisions.said: Access policies should be split into read and write where that applies (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app shows a capability whose ops part into reading and changing as two rules, Read and Write, each Everybody, Nobody or chosen members, under the capability's name; Write lets a member read too. Split: Emission Browser (watch / drive), Agent Management (see a chat and its transcript / send, answer, stop and change it), Kubernetes (get, list, logs / delete), Subscriptions (see accounts and usage / sign in or out, add, switch), Access Rules (see the rules / change them and the host's own admin). Not split, as nothing in them reads apart from using: Shell, Providers, Model Files and Databases (read-only through the mesh), Agent Spawn. Read and Write keep the old rule's defaults: Everybody, but Access Rules' Write, Nobody; Access Rules' Read is Everybody, as reading the rules always was. A rule kept before the split becomes both sides (Access Rules': Write)

parts.name: Meta's rows
parts.shows: Meta has a setting for each rule (access_<rule>: access_shell, access_kube_read, access_kube_write, …), read on every host of the mesh, in its index as "<host>: <rule>; …" (everybody, nobody, or chosen: the members' names), looked up off the main loop. Meta may set a rule narrower itself ([<host>:] nobody, or chosen with fewer members); a wider one it shows for the user. Shown under a reply (show setting:access_<rule>), it is a row for each host titled "<host> / <capability>", the same row as Settings: one button, or Read and Write for a split capability, greyed where that host's Access Rules refuse this one.

decisions.said: Meta should help configure access and show UI for the altered attributes, like a row of the host and the capability with a dropdown (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta can show a host's access rule as a "<host> / <capability>" row with its dropdown; the rule is the user's to change there

decisions.said: Meta may narrow a rule itself; widening shows the row for the user to flip; rows for any mesh host, not only this machine's (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Meta narrows access rules on any host itself and shows the row for a wider one; it never widens one

decisions.said: Access policies should be split into read and write where that applies (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta has a setting per rule, a split capability's Read and Write each one, and shows the capability's whole row (both lines) under its reply

states: default: every rule Everybody, Read and Write alike (Subscriptions too), but Access Rules' Write, Nobody (a mesh with no rules works as before; only this machine's heads, and those over ssh, change the rules till members are chosen; every member may read them)
error: the host's error in one dim row
no members: "No other members" under Everybody in the list
